contentEn:
Whole-house renovation costs in Metro Vancouver in 2026 range from $23,000 to over $300,000, depending on scope, finishes, and whether the work is cosmetic or structural. Reno Stars has completed projects in Vancouver and Richmond priced from $23,000 to $28,000 for scoped whole-house updates. This guide breaks down real costs, permit requirements for the City of Vancouver and BC, typical timelines, and how to plan your budget before you sign a contract.

What Does a Whole-House Renovation Cost in Vancouver?

The single most common question homeowners ask is: how much will my whole-house renovation actually cost? The honest answer in Metro Vancouver in 2026 is that costs fall across a wide range, and every project is different. A minor whole-house refresh — fresh paint, updated fixtures, new flooring — starts around $15,000 to $40,000. More comprehensive work that involves kitchen and bathroom remodels, rewiring, and plumbing updates typically lands between $35,000 and $150,000. A full structural renovation or complete rebuild in Metro Vancouver can exceed $150,000 to $300,000, depending on the size of the home and the quality of finishes selected.

Material costs in BC are subject to a 7% GST charge on most purchases, and labour for licensed trades — electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians — adds significant line items to any renovation budget. Reno Stars provides a detailed, itemized quote before any work begins, so homeowners know exactly what they are paying for.

Permits Required for Renovations in Vancouver and BC

Most whole-house renovations in Metro Vancouver require one or more permits from the City of Vancouver or the applicable municipality. A building permit is mandatory for any structural work - removing or adding walls, changing the building footprint, or modifying load-bearing elements. Electrical upgrades requiring a permit in BC include new panel installations, service upgrades exceeding 200 amps, and any new circuits in kitchens or bathrooms. Plumbing permits cover new drain connections, water heater replacements, and backflow prevention devices. Adding a secondary suite or laneway house requires both a building permit and a zoning review.

In the City of Vancouver, a heritage registry home may require Heritage Conservation Branch approval before exterior changes are permitted. Reno Stars manages permit applications as part of its standard project management service and has experience navigating City of Vancouver, Richmond, Surrey, and Burnaby requirements.

How Long Does a Whole-House Renovation Take in Metro Vancouver?

Timeline expectations in Metro Vancouver in 2026 vary by project scope. A minor whole-house refresh typically takes 6 to 12 weeks from permit approval to final inspection. More involved projects with kitchen and bathroom remodels run 12 to 24 weeks. A complete whole-house renovation that includes structural changes, mechanical upgrades, and a full finish-out requires 4 to 6 months on average. Full rebuilds or major additions in the City of Vancouver typically require 8 to 12 months, accounting for permit timelines, Heritage Vancouver reviews where applicable, and city inspection availability.

Reno Stars assigns a dedicated project manager to every renovation. That manager is the single point of contact from the first site visit through handover, keeping homeowners informed at every stage.

Financing Options for Home Renovations in BC

Whole-house renovations are significant investments. Homeowners in BC have several common financing paths. A home equity line of credit (HELOC) leverages the equity built up in a property at typically lower interest rates than personal loans. RBC, TD, and BMO all offer renovation loan products tailored to homeowners undertaking major repairs or upgrades. Some choose to finance in stages, paying for each phase as work is completed and inspected. Reno Stars works with clients on payment schedules tied to project milestones, so large lump sums are not required upfront.

How to Choose a Renovation Contractor in Metro Vancouver

The contractor you choose matters as much as the budget you set. In British Columbia, any contractor performing residential work for compensation is required to hold a valid BC residential builder licence under the Home Protection Act. Ask for the licence number and verify it through the BC Consumer Protection Office online registry before signing anything. Request proof of commercial general liability insurance - a reputable contractor carries no less than $2 million in coverage. Obtain at least three itemized quotes that specify materials, brand names, quantities, and labour rates. Quotes that list only a single lump sum are a warning sign. References from recently completed projects in your municipality are non-negotiable.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the average cost of a whole-house renovation in Vancouver in 2026?

In Metro Vancouver in 2026, a comprehensive whole-house renovation typically costs between $35,000 and $150,000 depending on size, scope, and finish level. Basic scoped updates start around $23,000 to $40,000. Full structural rebuilds in the City of Vancouver commonly run $150,000 to $300,000 or more. Reno Stars has completed projects in Vancouver and Richmond priced from $23,000 to $28,000 for scoped updates.

How long does a whole-house renovation take in Metro Vancouver?

A minor whole-house refresh takes 6 to 12 weeks. Kitchen and bathroom-focused remodels run 12 to 24 weeks. A complete whole-house renovation with structural changes requires 4 to 6 months. Full rebuilds or major additions in Vancouver typically take 8 to 12 months when permits, inspections, and Heritage reviews are included.

Do I need a building permit for a whole-house renovation in Vancouver?

Yes, for any structural work - removing or adding walls, changing the footprint, or modifying load-bearing elements. Electrical upgrades, new plumbing connections, and basement suite conversions also require permits in the City of Vancouver. Cosmetic work like painting and flooring typically does not require a permit. Reno Stars manages all permit applications as part of its project management service.
